Arm Newsroom
News
News
November 4, 2026
Arm delivers a record second quarter, reaching $1.44 billion in total revenue
Arm Q2 FYE27 quarterly earnings mark fifth consecutive quarter of total revenue growth exceeding 20% year over year.
Share
Today (November 4, 2026), Arm (NASDAQ: ARM) published a letter to its shareholders containing the company’s results for its second quarter of fiscal year 2027, which ended September 30, 2026. The infographic below provides the key highlights for the quarter:
Here are what the results mean and how they were achieved:
Total revenue for Arm in Q2 FYE27 increased 27% year over year to $1.44 billion
, representing Arm’s highest ever second quarter. This reflects strong execution and growing demand for the Arm compute platform.
Record second quarter was driven by
strong licensing and other revenue of $773 million
, reflecting a
50% year over year increase
, an important leading indicator of future royalty growth. Meanwhile, royalty revenue for the quarter reached $670 million, with
data center royalties doubling year over year
.
For the first time, Arm’s partners reported more than
10 billion Arm-based chips
shipped during the quarter – an increase of
1.5 billion chips year over year
– adding to the scale of the platform already used by
more than 30 million developers
.
Arm’s business is driven by two areas – both built on the same Arm compute platform, leveraging a common software ecosystem – that are seeing rapid growth as AI increases the amount and complexity of compute required across every market:
The IP business, where partners are increasing investment in Arm technology and deploying record numbers of Arm-based silicon; and
The new silicon business, where demand for the
Arm AGI CPU
is extremely strong.
Arm AGI CPU expands the business opportunity by delivering Arm-design silicon directly to customers, with demand continuing to strengthen:
Arm’s confidence in achieving
up to $2 billion in Arm AGI CPU revenue over FYE27 and FYE28
has increased over the past 90 days, supported by additional supply and customer mix.
Purchase orders for Arm AGI CPU have been secured from multiple customers extending through calendar 2027, and the first commercial deliveries are on track for Q4 FYE27.
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) announced
plans to offer Arm AGI CPU instances in 2027.
Independent testing by Signal65 showed Arm AGI CPU
delivering approximately
2x the performance per rack
versus AMD EPYC 9755.
Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers more than tripled – from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in calendar 2025. Based on current ramps across AWS Graviton, Google Axion, Microsoft Cobalt, and NVIDIA platforms,
Arm expects that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026
:
Amazon recently reported that Arm-based Graviton revenue commitments increased more than 20x year-over-year.
Google identified Arm-based Axion as a critical component of its AI infrastructure.
Microsoft highlighted strong adoption of Arm-based Cobalt CPUs.
NVIDIA continues to expand its Arm-based Vera CPU platform for agentic AI, with it now generally available on OCI and deployed in production with OpenAI.
Arm introduced
Arm Neoverse CSS N4
, enabling partners to develop differentiated silicon CPUs, networking, infrastructure management, and security, and delivering up to
2x performance per socket and 25% better performance per watt
than the prior generation.
Arm compute sits on both sides of the trust boundary for agentic AI, with NVIDIA’s recently announced OpenShell architecture using Arm-based CPUs to execute AI workloads, and Arm-based BlueField-4 DPUs to independently enforce security and isolation.
Arm-based PCs have now reached approximately 20% of global PC shipments
, reflecting the
growing adoption of Arm in personal computing
.
A new portfolio of PCs powered by
NVIDIA’s Arm-based RTX Spark
further expands Arm’s reach into local AI, content creation, and gaming for PC.
Google introduced Googlebook, a new category of AI-native laptops designed for Gemini Intelligence, with Arm serving as a primary compute platform for many models.
In smartphones,
Arm CSS for Mobile 2
drives the performance of
agentic AI workloads up by 70%
through
Arm Scalable Matrix Extension 2 (SME2)
, which is already adopted by major smartphone vendors like OPPO and vivo. Meanwhile,
Arm Mali G2-Ultra NX
, Arm’s first AI-native GPU, delivers up to
4x the frame rate at the same sustained power
, with Xiaomi adopting the technology, and leading game developers and engines integrating
Arm Neural Technology
.
Physical AI royalty revenue grew 50% year over year
, driven by increased adoption of advanced driver-assistance and in-vehicle infotainment systems expanding into more vehicles.
As vehicles become more intelligent and autonomous, demand for compute performance, real-time control, safety and security continues to increase, with Armv9 and
Arm Zena CSS
providing the foundation for this transition.
Arm launched Arm Total Design for Physical AI
, bringing together more than 80 companies across compute, software, AI models, and system integration, to accelerate the development and deployment of physical AI systems.
The full letter to shareholders is available on the Arm investor relations website (
https://investors.arm.com/financials/quarterly-annual-results
). Information about the Arm earnings conference call can be found
here
.
Forward-looking statements
This blog post contains forward-looking statements regarding Arm’s future performance, market opportunity, and customer demand. These statements are based on current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. For a discussion of factors that could affect Arm’s results, please refer to Arm’s filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Salesforce’s Agentforce Coworker Usage Soars 21x in Three Months as Enterprises Delegate Real Work to AI
November 4, 2026
6 min read
More than 185,000 users are putting Coworker to work, with companies including The Adecco Group, Fulton Bank, and BACA Systems expanding adoption across their businesses.
New capabilities make Coworker smarter, more proactive, and available wherever employees work — from Microsoft Teams to mobile and desktop.
Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), the world’s #1 AI CRM, today announced a major expansion of
Agentforce Coworker
, bringing new AI capabilities, deeper business context, and new experiences across Microsoft Teams, mobile, and desktop — building on 21x growth in usage in just three months. With reusable Skills, employees can rely on proven workflows instead of starting from scratch or wondering whether AI will get the job right. Conversation History lets them pick up where they left off, while upcoming scheduled tasks keep work moving without constant follow-up. At $50 per user per month, pricing is simple and predictable, which makes it easier for enterprises to expand adoption with confidence.
Built on decades of customer relationships, business processes, and trusted enterprise data, Coworker puts the full power of Salesforce to work from day one. Drawing on existing Salesforce records, business metadata, and connected data through
Data 360
, it brings together specialized
Agentforce
agents and workflows to help employees get meaningful work done. Customers can get started in minutes, with the security, permissions, and governance they already trust—and now bring that power into the tools they use every day.
Give it a job; Agentforce Coworker helps get it done
Agentforce Coworker is Salesforce’s AI teammate that helps employees delegate business work using trusted Salesforce context. Instead of navigating multiple applications or figuring out which Agentforce agents to use, employees can start with the job they need done.
Coworker helps plan the steps, coordinate the right Agentforce agents and workflows, and bring back results and recommended actions for review.
For example, a seller can ask Coworker to investigate an at-risk renewal. Coworker can help pull together relevant service history, identify unresolved cases, prepare customer follow-up, and coordinate supported actions across the appropriate agents and workflows.
And because Coworker already knows existing Salesforce data, metadata, and permissions, customers can begin putting it to work without starting from scratch.
“The next era of
enterprise AI
isn’t about giving users more agents to manage,” said James Nakashima, SVP, Product Management, Salesforce. “It’s about giving them one Coworker that brings the right agents together to get work done. What makes this powerful for Salesforce customers is that Coworker starts with their business context, works within the security and permissions they already trust, and can be up and running in minutes. That’s how we make AI practical for every user.”
Built for the way enterprises work
Getting real business work done requires more than an intelligent model. It requires relevant customer information, business processes, and the ability to take appropriate action within established controls.
Coworker brings these capabilities together through Salesforce.
It can draw on existing Salesforce customer relationships, records, metadata, and supported connected data sources, including
Data 360
. It can coordinate supported Agentforce agents, flows, and business actions to help employees complete multi-step assignments.
Moreover, Coworker is designed to operate within Salesforce’s established security and governance framework, using applicable employee permissions, sharing rules, and configured access controls. Organizations can manage access to supported agents and actions, with approval and audit capabilities available for supported operations.
For Salesforce customers, this means they can start with the business foundation they’ve already built rather than beginning with a separate AI implementation.
What’s new today
Delegate without leaving Microsoft Teams.
Coworker now meets employees where their work day happens. Hand it a job in a Teams conversation, and it brings the same Salesforce context, permissions, and governance, coordinates the right Agentforce agents, and turns the conversation into action without switching apps. A seller can delegate a deal review, and a service manager can have it dig into an escalation, right from a chat.
See the whole customer story.
Customer details live in more places than the CRM. With new Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 connections, Coworker pairs the email, calendars, and files around every account with Salesforce data. A meeting brief or a renewal plan reflects the complete customer story, not just what’s in the CRM.
Work from any device.
New iOS, Mac, and Windows apps keep work moving at the desk or on the go. Delegate a job from your laptop, track its progress from your phone, and review results and approve actions from any device.
Pick up where you left off.
With Conversation History, you can continue a conversation without starting over, across Salesforce, Microsoft Teams, and the new apps. Start a job in the morning and come back to it from another device, with the context intact.
Turn know-how into the team’s standard.
With Skills, a proven workflow becomes a one-line request anyone on the team can run. A top rep’s renewal playbook, for example, becomes how the whole team runs renewals.
Work that keeps going.
Starting in December, scheduled tasks handle recurring work, so results are waiting when you return. Daily Digest greets you each morning with your top priorities, so you know where to focus before you open your inbox.
Predictable pricing.
A new $50 per-user, per-month option makes Coworker easier to budget as adoption grows. Teams can start small, measure the value, and expand with confidence.

Your AI Agents Are Fast. Your Process Isn’t. Here’s How to Fix It.
6 min read
From rapid adoption to real business impact
From financial services to professional services and manufacturing, organizations are deploying Coworker quickly and finding practical ways to use it across their teams.
Fulton Bank: From zero to 20+ production use cases in weeks.
Fulton Bank deployed more than 20 Coworker use cases supporting approximately 3,000 users.
“Agentforce Coworker has been a game changer for Fulton Bank. We’re already seeing substantial daily usage and real examples of how Coworker is helping teammates find information faster, prepare more effectively, and move work forward,” said Brandon Bernard, Senior Vice President/Sales Technology Strategist, Fulton Bank
The Adecco Group: Bringing business context into everyday work.
Adecco is expanding Coworker across 40 countries, helping employees access relevant candidate and client information when it matters.
“The launch of Agentforce Coworker means our teams have access to a single interface that understands candidate history and client context precisely when human judgment matters most,” said Denis Machuel, CEO, The Adecco Group
BACA Systems: Getting started in 20 minutes.
BACA enabled Coworker in an environment with 1,300 custom objects and began using it to answer questions that previously required extensive manual searching.
“It answered questions that just yesterday would have been 45–60 mins of swivel-chairing between screens and systems,” said Andrew Russo, VP of Business Systems, BACA Systems
Together, these examples demonstrate the potential for enterprises to adopt Coworker quickly, make existing business information more accessible, and put specialized AI capabilities into everyday workflows.
Availability
Available now:
Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 connectivity; Conversation History; Skills; the per-user, per-month SKU.
Generally available in November 2026
: Agentforce Coworker in Microsoft Teams; Agentforce Coworker app for iOS; Agentforce Coworker desktop app for Mac and Windows; Coworker MCP server for connectivity; free trial for Flex Credits customers.
Expected in December 2026:
Daily Digest; Scheduled tasks; Agentforce Coworker in the Field Service, Consumer Goods Cloud, and Life Sciences Cloud mobile apps.
Get started
Salesforce customers can turn on Agentforce Coworker in Setup today. To give every user a Coworker with per-user pricing, contact your Salesforce account executive.

Half of Slack Messages Are No Longer From People. Here’s Slack by the Numbers.
November 3, 2026
2 min read
More than a decade ago an engineering team built
Slack
because they needed a way to coordinate code, log alerts, and talk to each other all in one place. Now, as
AI agents
move from pilots into live business production, they’ve entered the channels where people already collaborate: Through open standards like MCP, agents can pull context from Slack across platforms like GitHub, Salesforce, and Jira to take direct action in real time. Slack now processes 127 million of these automated actions, called MCP tool calls, every week, a figure that is doubling quarter over quarter.
Today, at Anthropic alone,
65% of all code changes ship through Slack
, and users send a billion messages on the platform every day.
Six years after Slack joined Salesforce, we’re sharing some data that shows how Slack’s origin in humans and software working side by side became the execution layer for humans and agents working together.
Scale and momentum
Over 100,000 customers have joined Slack so far in 2026.

To keep pace with demand across billions of semiconductor devices,
Rochester Electronics
uses Slack as an operational command center where humans and automated workflows work side by side. The company has seen rapid adoption of Slackbot and reusable Skills, empowering employees to instantly generate executive briefings, prep for customer meetings, and conduct sales performance analysis from one place. Combined with custom Slack workflows that automate routine administrative tasks and surface critical Salesforce notifications, Rochester has removed daily operational friction and turned conversations into fast execution.
Some tasks feel like stopping at a traffic light every few minutes of a journey. The journey shouldn’t take that long, but you get stuck at every red light. Slack helps us remove those obstacles that stop the flow of work.
Colin Strother, Executive Vice President, Rochester Electronics

Decisions from engineering to go-to-market happen in public channels, and hundreds of Slack Connect channels give customers and partners a direct line to the team. Employees search Slack more than 250,000 times a month, and transparent communication eliminates more than 70,000 hours of meetings a year. Vercel also runs agents in Slack. Its inbound sales agent lets one rep handle lead qualification, research, and outreach drafting that would otherwise take a team of 10. And now as a Slack Code launch partner, Vercel is extending that model to software development, bringing its agent into code channels where whole teams build together.
“At Vercel, everything starts in Slack. It’s our power grid for operations,” said Matt Lewis, Partner Sales Engineer at Vercel.
